![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221961/assets/8aed400e7768b70f4532642418d83b36d9e32aa84db87c71ea6d902504930bc4.png)

Consider the vector field $F(x,y)$ shown above, and let $C$ be the path where the semiellipse is traversed from $A$ to $B.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$

II. ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0$

III. ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ gives the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along $C:$

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- If the force works *against* the motion  of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statement I is false, while statement II is true. Since the force $F$ acts perpendicular to the motion of the particle as it moves from $A$ to $B,$ it neither helps nor hinders its motion. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221961/assets/d8e05de34bf9ddfdbf9580b1df32eb9e091f56f76ac3616cbb1cd81d5d212a86.png)

 
So, ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0.$

- Statement III is true. If we reverse the orientation of $C,$ then the situation with regards to the work done by $F$ is similar to the previous case.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221961/assets/17423916013677c1476df5a4368ab9eec81671b04b4ca29a0e702b20ddc818f2.png)

 
So, ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
